problem:
Title: N over Pi times Reciprocal of 1 Plus n Squared x Squared Delta Sequence/Proof 1

[[File:LorDeltaSequence.png|thumb|600px|The graph of the $\ds \frac n \pi \frac 1 {1 + n^2 x^2}$ delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the graph becomes thinner and taller. The area under each graph is equal to $1$.]]
Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a [[Definition:Sequence|sequence]] such that:

:$\map {\delta_n} x := \frac n \pi \frac 1 {1 + n^2 x^2}$

Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a [[Definition:Delta Sequence|delta sequence]].

That is, in the [[Definition:Schwartz Distribution|distributional]] sense it holds that:

:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {\delta_n} x = \map \delta x$

or

:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map {\delta_n} x \map \phi x \rd x = \map \delta \phi$

where:
:$\phi \in \map \DD \R$ is a [[Definition:Test Function|test function]]
:$\delta$ is the [[Definition:Dirac Delta Distribution|Dirac delta distribution]]
:$\map \delta x$ is the [[Definition:Abuse of Notation|abuse of notation]], usually interpreted as an infinitely thin and tall spike with its area equal to $1$.
